records.body:
## Why it qualifies

Five consecutive bridge structures, ~1.8km of them, replaced under one contract while traffic keeps running. Construction began January 2026 with completion late 2029 — the pour programme is almost entirely ahead.

The repeatability is the argument. This is not one bridge; it is five broadly comparable structures built in sequence by the same team, plus interchange works. A striking-time saving proved on the first structure carries straight into the next four.

## Concrete scope

- Five bridge structures spanning the Ruhr, the Rhein-Herne-Kanal, a Duisburg harbour basin, a DB line and a park
- Deep foundations over and beside water
- ~2km of A59 widened to six lanes; A40/A59 interchange rebuilt with new overpasses
- Phased construction: new structure west of the existing alignment first, then demolition and replacement

## Entry angle

Lead on cycle time across the five structures rather than monitoring in the abstract. The stronger commercial point is that Hochtief Infrastructure's regional team is simultaneously running the A40 Rheinbrücke Neuenkamp second structure and the A1 Leverkusen eight-lane widening — three concurrent large-pour schemes within about 40km. That is an account conversation, not a project conversation.

## Gaps

No named site team found in public sources. Other ARGE members are not published. Frame self-delivery is inferred from Hochtief's pattern on Neuenkamp, not confirmed for this contract.

## Sources

- World Construction Network / Yahoo Finance — Hochtief-led JV award, ~EUR450m, scope, dates
- Hochtief corporate statements on the Ruhr region infrastructure portfolio

The composite deck on the approach spans is poured in Taktschieben segments, which is genuinely repeatable, and two 75m pylons remain to build. What pulls this down from High is sequence: the 532m longitudinal launch completed in March 2026 and the remaining work is dominated by pylon erection and Freivorbau steel over the river rather than by repeated concrete cycles. Part of the eight-lane A40 widening between Duisburg-Homberg and Duisburg-Häfen. Completion reported as 2028, having slipped from 2026.

records.body:
## Why it qualifies

Germany's largest cable-stayed bridge, built twice. The second structure is under construction beside the first, which opened in November 2023, using the same method under harder constraints — no provisional arrangements are possible this time because the first bridge is carrying live A40 traffic.

## Concrete scope

- Approach spans in Stahl-Beton-Verbund, deck poured segmentally behind the Taktschieben launch
- Two 75m pylons still to erect
- Free-cantilever deck over the Rhine main span
- Transverse shift of the completed south structure, 14.4m including pylons

## Honest read on timing

This is the weakness. The 532m longitudinal launch finished in March 2026 and what remains is steel-led: pylons, then free cantilever. A material share of the deck concrete is already placed. It is a Medium because of sequence, not because of scope.

## Entry angle

Don't pursue this standalone. The same Hochtief Infrastructure regional team runs the A59 Berliner Brückenzug (started Jan 2026, whole programme ahead) and the A1 Leverkusen widening. Lead with the A59 and let Neuenkamp be the credibility reference — Hochtief already knows what the pours cost them here.

## Gaps

No capital value published for the second structure alone. Completion date reported as 2028 but not confirmed by DEGES in any source found. No site-level contacts indexed.

## Sources

- SOLID / solidbau.at — ARGE composition, dimensions, steel tonnage, launch dates
- DEGES project page and progress releases
- EHS beratende Ingenieure — supervision scope

records.body:
## Why it qualifies

A six-lane replacement viaduct in procurement right now, with a Baustart targeted for the end of 2026. No Planfeststellungsverfahren is needed — the Genehmigungsbeschleunigungsgesetz lets it run as a maintenance measure — so it is moving faster than a comparable scheme would.

On its own it is a moderate bridge. Its value is that it is the nearest open door into the A45 programme.

## The programme behind it

The A45 Sauerlandlinie carries 73 viaducts between Dortmund and Gießen; 60 are being replaced. Twelve are finished, ten are in construction, and the programme runs to at least 2035 under a single client — Autobahn GmbH, Niederlassung Westfalen. NRW has already let 24 bridge replacements on **funktionale Ausschreibung**, where the offered construction time is a scored award criterion alongside price, and 28 more using Schnellbauweisen.

That procurement model is the commercial hook. When bid construction time is scored, anything that shortens the pour-to-strike cycle affects whether a contractor wins, not just their margin afterwards.

## Entry angle

Go at the client, not the bridge. The contractor for Büschergrund is not appointed, so there is nobody on the delivery side to sell to yet — but Autobahn NL Westfalen specifies the method and scores the bids for sixty of these. Rahmede is the reference to lead with: it came in about half a year early on a funktional award.

## Gaps

No contractor, no published value, no bridge dimensions found. Record deliberately kept honest about that — the band is driven by timing and programme access, not by verified scope.

## Sources

- Siegener Zeitung, Feb 2026 — Vergabeverfahren under way, no Planfeststellung required
- Autobahn GmbH, Mar 2026 — Büschergrund Startschuss expected end of year
- Autobahn GmbH project pages — 60 of 73 viaducts, 12 complete, 10 in build

Three hyperscale data centre campuses going up in parallel in the Rheinisches Revier, with construction only just started. Two hooks, and they are independent of each other.

**No general contractor is published in any source I could find.** Microsoft is the developer, Westnetz has the grid works, and the municipalities issued the permits — but nobody has named the builder. ## Why it qualifies

Germany's largest industrial decarbonisation project, and PORR — a named Lisa account — holds the foundation package through PORR Spezialtiefbau in ARGE with Implenia.

- Frankipfähle and CMC soil-improvement columns across a 40-football-pitch site
- One of the main base slabs for the 140m DR tower
- 14m-deep excavation with a 4,200m2 watertight enclosure and Ortbeton diaphragm walls
- 60+ structures across the complex

## Honest read on timing

This is why it is a Medium and not a High. Tiefbau started in mid-2024. By June 2026 the foundations were reported as largely prepared and pile-stabilised, with roads and services in. SMS began erecting the tower in February 2026 and commissioning starts in 2027.

The thick-section, high-consequence concrete — the thing Cure and Signal are actually for — is substantially behind us on this phase.

## Entry angle

Don't sell this phase. Use it. PORR Spezialtiefbau is on site and is an existing target account for Lisa in Continental Europe; the natural conversation is what remains across the 60+ ancillary structures, and what the next tkH2Steel phase looks like. thyssenkrupp has committed to full transformation by 2045, so there is more DRI capacity coming — it is just not publicly programmed yet.

The MixAI angle is real but oddly placed: the whole project exists to cut CO2, so embodied carbon in the concrete is rhetorically awkward for them to ignore, even though the driver is process emissions rather than materials.

## Gaps

No published breakdown of remaining concrete. No programme for later phases. The EUR3bn figure is total investment including plant — it is in the Value field because it is the published project cost, but it must not be quoted as a construction value.

records.body:
## Why it qualifies

Lock chambers are about as close to a textbook mass-concrete case as exists: very thick walls and base slabs, watertightness required for a design life measured in generations, and severe consequences if early-age cracking gets into the structure.

Here the same client is replacing them at **three sites to one design**, and construction has not been tendered yet.

## Concrete scope

- Three replacement lock chambers on the Wesel-Datteln-Kanal, plus lock bridges, forebays and pumping stations
- Thick sections throughout, watertight construction
- Shared design across sites, so pour methodology repeats

## Entry angle

This is a specification play, not a contractor play — there is no contractor to sell to yet, which is precisely the point. Two addressable parties:

1. **WNA Datteln** as the client. They also hold the DEK-Nord new locks (Bevergern starting spring 2026, Rodde) and the Datteln-Hamm-Kanal Oststrecke locks at Hamm and Werries. One client relationship covers a decade of lock construction across NRW.
2. **The Sweco / WTM Engineers / GRBV Ingenieurgemeinschaft**, who are writing the specification now.

## Context that helps the pitch

The WDK is the busiest German waterway after the Rhine — over 20,000 vessels a year through Friedrichsfeld — and it is the only waterborne supply route to the Marl chemical complex. Outage risk during replacement is a serious operational constraint, which makes construction sequencing and confidence in early strength commercially significant rather than a technical nicety.

## Gaps

No contractors, no tender dates, no chamber dimensions, no value. The EUR1.5bn number that appears in press coverage is the ten-year Westdeutsches Kanalnetz action plan across roughly 200 projects — not this one, and it must not be attached to this record.

## Sources

- WNA Datteln — W23 project page, BVWP classification
- Sweco GmbH and WTM Engineers, 2023 — Ingenieurgemeinschaft appointment and scope
- Wikipedia / SkipperGuide — WDK traffic volumes, six stages, 40m lift
- Recklinghäuser Zeitung — Westdeutsches Kanalnetz action plan context

Two replacement lock chambers plus up to eight bridge replacements along an 11.5km canal section, all within the city of Hamm and all under one client. - Schleuse Hamm: existing 86m usable length, 9.40m chamber width, 1.65m lift
- Schleuse Werries: existing 93m usable, 11.50m width, 5.30m lift

## Honest read on timing

The scope is real and the priority classification is real, but nothing suggests it is close. No construction dates are published anywhere I could find, and the authority's own project pages were reported as partly still carrying February 2022 information as of April 2026.

That is a different situation from "no date published yet" — it suggests the section is not being actively progressed at the pace of Bevergern or the WDK works.

## Why it qualifies

Four new underground stations and connecting tunnel beneath central Cologne. On scope alone this is one of the largest urban concrete programmes in the state — deep excavations, diaphragm walls, thick base slabs and tunnel linings in dense historic ground.

## Why it is only a Medium

Timing. The Rat decided for the tunnel in April 2025, but the Innenstadt works cannot be tendered until roughly mid-2028 after a two-year approval process, with execution from about mid-2029 — and that is explicitly conditional on the funding award. No Baubeschluss has been taken.

The surface sections move earlier: West from mid-2026, East from mid-2027.

## Concrete scope

- Underground stations at Heumarkt, Neumarkt, Rudolfplatz and Moltkestraße
- Connecting tunnel, plus Vorhaltebauwerke for a later Rhine crossing to Deutz and a westward extension
- Right-bank works: fire-safety upgrades and two new exits per station from Deutz Technische Hochschule to Fuldaer Straße, step-free access at all 17 right-bank stops

## Entry angle

Too early to work, but not too early to note. Cologne carries institutional memory of the Nord-Sued Stadtbahn — the 2009 archive collapse — which makes monitoring and evidence around deep urban excavation a far easier conversation here than it would be elsewhere. That is worth holding for the specification window in 2027-28.

Two distinct client bodies to track: Stadt Köln's Amt für Brücken, Tunnel und Stadtbahnbau on the left bank, KVB on the right.

## Gaps

No Baubeschluss, no value, no contractors, no funding confirmation. Line 9's routing is still a Prüfauftrag.

## Sources

- Stadt Köln — Ost-West-Achse project pages and programme dates
- ostwestachse.koeln — Innenstadt scope, Rat decision, Prüfaufträge
- KVB blog, Apr 2025 — Rat vote 49-14, no Baubeschluss yet

Rahmede was let on a **funktionale Ausschreibung**: planning and construction from one supplier, with the offered construction time scored as an award criterion alongside price. 453m steel composite structure at ~70m height, two halves, ~7,000t of steel, ~EUR170m. Launched from both abutments simultaneously, deck slab cast in sections by Pilgerschritt with a formwork carriage.

## Why it qualifies

The best-timed large project in this sweep, and the warmest.

11km twin-bore rail tunnel. €1.69bn, financing agreement signed December 2025, Baurecht granted the same month, preparatory earthworks started 9 February 2026. Roughly 10.8km driven bergmännisch, plus a 300m cut-and-cover section and 3.5km of surface line. The tunnel drive and lining are entirely ahead.

## Why access is unusually good

**STRABAG is a named Lisa account.** Züblin is a STRABAG group company, and Wayss & Freytag — which holds the tunnelling package jointly with Züblin — sits under BAM, also a named account. Three routes in, all warm.

## The alliance angle

This is the first DB megaproject delivered end-to-end under the **Partnerschaftsmodell Schiene** — a multi-party contract signed with all ten alliance partners rather than bilateral contracts, with everyone involved from design stage. STRABAG's own framing is "we win or lose together."

That matters commercially. The usual objection to cycle-time tooling is that a subcontractor carries no schedule risk, so the saving lands with someone else. In an alliance where outcomes are shared, a method improvement benefits every party at the table. It is a materially easier sale than the same conversation under a traditional contract.

## Gaps

Commissioning date is unsettled — DB and January 2026 coverage say end 2032, June 2026 reporting says December 2033. No pour programme published. No site team indexed.

## Why it qualifies

Around 55 buildings demolished and numerous new ones built at the Navy's Wilhelmshaven dockyard, running to the end of the 2030s. The state building authority calls it unique in Germany.

A decade-plus rolling programme under one client with repeated building types, at a moment when defence infrastructure funding is expanding.

## Why Medium, not High

Two honest reasons:

## Why it qualifies

The construction method does the work here.

A 1.1km twin-bore cut-and-cover tunnel built as a **sequence of separate excavation boxes, each around 200m long**. Main works started end January 2026; completion targeted end 2033. That is a long series of near-identical pours, almost entirely ahead — the textbook repeatability case.

**No contractor is named in any source I could find** — and main works have already started. That's unusual for a €1.5bn federal scheme and worth chasing directly: Autobahn GmbH NL West, or the vergabe.autobahn.de award archive.

## Why it qualifies

Design selected June 2026, construction **not yet procured**. That is precisely the pre-award moment where a monitoring requirement gets written into a specification rather than sold to a contractor afterwards.

## Why the urgency is real

From **May 2026** the 1974 bridge is closed to permit-requiring heavy transports over 44 tonnes. The port industry association (UVHH) is publicly describing "dramatic restrictions" and warning that further weight limits or a full HGV closure would cause logistical standstill across much of the port.

Current completion target is end of the 2030s. Industry says that's far too late and is pressing for acceleration. A client under that kind of public pressure is a client who will listen to anything that compresses programme.

## Concrete scope

## Why it qualifies

The legal position just improved materially. The Bundesverwaltungsgericht required the 2023 Planfeststellungsbeschluss to be corrected on **only two narrow points** — climate in the variant assessment, and water permits — explicitly not on traffic need or climate generally.

DEGES is implementing those corrections and pursuing a renewed decision. For a scheme that had been litigated, that's a significant narrowing.

## Concrete scope

New motorway through the port including the Süderelbe bridge, with sections 6a (A7/A26 to Moorburg), 6b (rising to the Süderelbe crossing) and 6c (Hohe Schaar to AD Süderelbe).

## Why Medium, not High

- No construction date; Erörterung for 6a only targeted from late 2026
- Environmental opposition remains active and argues for dropping the scheme entirely in favour of upgrading the Haupthafenroute
- **Budget tension**: Hamburg must fund roughly half the Köhlbrand crossing itself. The city's two largest port projects compete for the same money, and the Köhlbrandbrücke has the more urgent structural case

## Gaps

No construction start, value or main-works contractor. Only a supervision tender for section 6a.

## Sources

- DEGES Hafenpassage project page, Apr 2026 — BVerwG reasoning, corrections required, Erörterung timing
- hamburg.de BWAI — section 6a and 6c Planfeststellung records
- NABU Hamburg — opposition case and the Köhlbrand funding point

## Why it qualifies

The most reputationally loaded bridge project in Germany, and the specification is being written right now.

The 2024 collapse made prestressed concrete durability a national issue — it is the direct reason the Berlin Mühlendammbrücke and Elsenbrücke records exist in this sweep. Structural monitoring and evidence carry weight here that they simply would not on an ordinary replacement.

## The window, and it is unusually well published

- 18 Aug 2026 — Begleitgremium recommends LAP + Knight Architects, 14 votes to 12
- **3 Sep 2026 — Stadtrat decides**
- End Sep 2026 — Planungsstufe 2 begins
- Early 2027 — approval-ready design
- Oct 2027 — construction tender
- May 2028 — construction starts

That's a fourteen-month run-up during which the client decides what to specify. After October 2027 the conversation moves to a contractor who has already priced the method.

## Why the conversation can be technical

A named academic expert panel under **Prof. Steffen Marx (TU Dresden)** is advising the process. That makes a serious engineering discussion possible rather than a commercial pitch — and Marx is a structural concrete specialist, which is the right audience.

## Caveat on freshness

The Stadtrat votes on **3 September 2026** — days after this record was written. Confirm the outcome before acting; the design team named here may change.

## Sources

## Why it qualifies

The largest urban civils programme in Rheinland-Pfalz, and the timing has just turned.

That was the stated precondition for demolishing the **Hochstraße Nord** — 34 individual bridges of up to 70m span across about 2km, built 1970–81 — and replacing it with the at-grade Helmut-Kohl-Allee plus an entirely new city quarter.

Demolition starts at the north bridgehead from 2026. Beyond that: years of new road and quarter construction on cleared land.

## The proof point the client already owns

The Süd phase was: bored piles, base slabs, then **43 piers and 39 foundations** — delivered inside three years after seven years of public disruption.

This is a client who has just measured what a compressed urban rebuild actually costs them, and is about to start a bigger one. That's an unusually good moment to be in the room.

No contractor published for the Nord phase. No values. No Helmut-Kohl-Allee construction dates.

Date conflict on the Süd reopening — one source says early 2026, another 3 July 2026. Both recorded.

## Why it qualifies

A new Rhine crossing is large concrete by any measure, and the design is being settled right now — preliminary design was due to complete in the first half of 2026, with Planfeststellung applications to follow on both sides of the river.

Ground investigation is complete and the geotechnical report has been available since early 2024, so the technical basis exists. This is a live specification opportunity, not an abstraction.

## Why Medium

Planfeststellung across two Länder, for a scheme first studied in **1999**, is a long road. No construction date. Variant selection was still open at the time of the source.

## The practical first step

## Why it qualifies

The cleanest rerun in the entire German sweep.

A ~1,500m twin bridge over the Kiel Canal, built in two halves. The eastern half was let at **€307m** to an Implenia-led consortium; by December 2025, 1,382 of 1,500 metres were in final position, and it opens mid-December 2026.

Then: old bridge demolished January 2027 to February 2028. Western half built **2028–2031** — and it is **not yet awarded**.

## Why that sequencing matters

A contractor is about to finish a large, technically demanding launched bridge, and then build a near-identical one on the same site.

When they bid the western half, they will do so with direct, measured cost data from the eastern half — including exactly what their pour and launch cycle cost them. That is the most receptive possible moment for a cycle-time conversation, and the tender is still ahead.

## The account reach

Implenia also appears on the **Munich 2. Stammstrecke Ostbahnhof tunnel** (50/50 with Hochtief) and the **Duisburg tkH2Steel foundations** (ARGE with PORR) in this sweep. Three records, one account.

## Honest caveat

DEGES states the 2028–2031 western programme depends on "continuous, demand-appropriate financing." Planned, not committed. And the western half sits on the old alignment — ground conditions may not be identical to the eastern.

## Sources

- DEGES project page, Aug 2026 — consortium, €307m, phasing, dates

## The profile is outstanding — the location is not what it looks like

**89 precast tunnel elements, each ~73,500 tonnes**, cast in a purpose-built factory and floated out for immersion. That is a production line, not a construction site — the strongest repeatability profile anywhere in this sweep.

The casting factory is at **Rødbyhavn, in Denmark**. The repeated element production sits outside Schleswig-Holstein and outside the geography this sweep covers.

Construction began summer 2020 with completion in 2029, so element production is well advanced. A project of this scale and maturity very likely has established monitoring arrangements already — verify before approaching rather than assuming a clean field.

DEGES is upgrading the B207 between Heiligenhafen-Ost and Puttgarden including a new junction — a separate, smaller, and actually addressable piece of work.

## The best-quantified opportunity in the sweep

> **300,000 m³ of concrete and more than 100,000 tonnes of steel** for the entire construction project.

That figure comes from the European Commission's own technical description of POWER4STEEL, not a press release. It is the single most useful number produced by this entire German sweep.

For comparison: Infineon's Dresden fab used ~153,000 m³. This is roughly double, on one project.

## Timing

Excellent, and most of it is ahead:

- EAF commissioning **Q2 2028** and **Q2 2029**
- DRI plant commissioning **Q3 2029**
- Blast furnace closure 2030

## A named contractor already pouring

**WOLFF & MÜLLER** is building the water treatment plants for ROGESA at Dillingen: seven buildings on a 27,000 m² site, **~25,000 m³ of concrete**, centred on a Rundeindicker. Announced April 2026.

That is a named counterparty, on site, with a defined concrete package and a published volume. It is the cleanest entry point in the file.

## The rest of the scope

DRI plant, two EAF buildings, a hot link from DRI to EAF, cold DRI bins, a scrap yard, new electrical supply, slag treatment hall — several distinct structures across two sites under one client group. Real repeatability.

## Why MixAI is native here

This is Europe's largest steel decarbonisation project. Carbon in the construction is not an awkward add-on to the conversation; it is the entire premise of the project.

## Gaps

Civil contractors for the DRI plant and EAF buildings not all identified. The €3.5bn total is a 2023 estimate, not a construction contract.

## Sources

- wolff-mueller.de, Apr 2026 — water treatment package, 25,000 m³, seven buildings
- dillinger.de / home-of-steel.de — equipment awards, capacities, Pure Steel+ funding

**Now:** a €90m repair of the 550m A1 Weser bridge, running to end 2027, with traffic on one half at a time. Substantial in its own right.

It gives a natural reason to be in conversation with DEGES and with whoever holds the repair contract, well before the replacement is tendered. Being known before a major tender is worth more than reacting to it.

## Why it is recorded

Bremen's 2026 programme runs from the A1 in the east to the A270 in the north, with several multi-year schemes concurrent. Named elements: the A281 airport tunnel, the A1 Weser bridge repair, and Wilhelm-Kaisen-Brücke works.

As an aggregate it is a steady stream of structural work under a small number of client bodies in a compact city state — which makes an account approach unusually efficient here compared to a large Flächenland.

## Why Medium

The individually significant items are already recorded separately. What remains is smaller work with no published contractors or values.

## An explicit gap

**Bremerhaven is part of the Land Bremen and appears nowhere in these records.** It is a major port construction location and bremenports was not searched at all in this sweep.

That is a gap in the sweep, not an absence of activity. Container terminal and offshore terminal works there would be exactly the marine concrete profile that scored highly at Cuxhaven and Warnemünde. Worth a dedicated pass.
